group: Names found while generating translation batches (Ops 02-28)

entries.role: The in-universe 1970s-style super robot anime (full title ゲキ・ガンガー3) loved by Gai Daigoji and Akito; also the name of its robot.
entries.notes: Contested. The Nadesico wiki's page title is 'Gekigangar 3', but its own article body and category say 'Gekiganger III'. The SRW Wiki writes 'Gekigangar III' and uses bare 'Gekigangar' for the show. Wikipedia and the ADV dub use 'Gekiganger III' / 'Gekiganger 3'. Following the page-title rule gives 'Gekigangar'. The Japanese here drops the 3, so I dropped it too; use 'Gekigangar 3' for ゲキ・ガンガー3. NOTE: the project's existing personality notes (dragonar_nadesico.json) say 'Gekiganger'. Pick one spelling for the whole project.

entries.role: The otherworld between sea and land where Dunbine takes place.
entries.notes: SRW Wiki page title, Wikipedia, and the OVA title 'The Tale of Neo Byston Well' all agree.

entries.role: Drake Luft's flagship aura battleship; an enemy ship in Operation 25.
entries.notes: Variant katakana (small ィ) of the existing names.json key ウイル・ウィプス, which is 'Will Wipps'. The SRW Wiki lists it exactly as 'Will Wipps (ウィル・ウィプス)', and MAHQ and Akurasu's ACE2 flow chart also use 'Will Wipps'. Other spellings: 'Will-Wips' (Wikipedia), 'Will Wisp' (SRW character list).

entries.role: Aura battleship of Bishot Hatta, King of Ku; an enemy ship in Operation 25.
entries.notes: The SRW Wiki mecha list writes 'Gea Garing (ゲア・ガリング)', and so does the official Crusade System TCG card U-060. MAHQ and Akurasu's ACE2 flow chart write 'Gea Gring'. Other forms seen: 'Gea Galing'. No dedicated page exists. Chose the wiki spelling, matching how Goraon was chosen in dunbine_rean_brain.json.

entries.role: Evolved Antibody created by reviving a Grand Cher (e.g. Jonathan Baronz, Quincy Baronz).
entries.notes: This is NOT a Dunbine ship (the hint was wrong). It is the same word as バロンズゥ in the existing names.json entries ジョナサン・バロンズゥ = 'Jonathan Baronz' and クインシィ・バロンズゥ = 'Quincy Baronz', just with a dot. Kept 'Baronz' for consistency. Variant: 'Baronzu' (SRW Wiki).

entries.role: Class of Drake-side aura ship; a weaker cousin of the aura battleships.
entries.notes: The SRW Wiki mecha list ('Bull Beggar', an Aura Ship) and MAHQ ('Bull Beggar class') agree.

entries.role: Queen of the Ferario, who lives in the Land of Water. Late in the series she sends every Aura Machine and its crew up to the surface world, at the cost of her own life.
entries.personality: Aloof and self-centred; puts her own race and Byston Well first and does not care what harm comes to humans or the surface world. Her aura is overwhelming, almost godlike.
entries.notes: No English wiki page exists, and the SRW Wiki and Wikipedia character lists don't name her. 'Jacoba Aon' is the ADV dub credit (IMDb) and the TV Tropes spelling. A literal romanization gives 'Jakoba Aon'.

entries.ja: オペレーション・ライトニング
entries.role: Name of the operation that covers Operations 22 and 23 (22: Defeat Death Demon Corps; 23: Escort Friendly Detachment).
entries.notes: Akurasu's ACE2 flow chart titles both Op 22 and Op 23 'Operation Lightning'. It is a direct English loan, so there is no other reading.

entries.role: Poseidal-side planetary cruiser; Giwaza Lowau's flagship class. ACE2 Op 23 objective: 'Destroy Sarge Opus'.
entries.notes: It is from L-Gaim, not Layzner. Akurasu's ACE2 page and MAHQ write 'Sarge Opus'. The official English of SRW 30/Y writes 'Sarge Aupus'. The existing lgaim_layzner.json (Giwaza Fleet note) already uses 'Sarge Opus'.

entries.ja: オーガニック・プレート
entries.role: The disc-shaped plates Orphan produces, from which Antibodies are revived.
entries.notes: Wikipedia writes it lowercase ('an organic plate'). Capitalized to match the glossary's 'Organic Energy'. Also called 'B-Plate' (ビー・プレート).

entries.ja: オーガニック・エンジン
entries.role: Orphan's organic power source/engine.
entries.notes: mmecha writes it lowercase ('Orphan possesses an organic engine'). It is a direct English loan. Capitalized to match 'Organic Energy'.

entries.role: The living organic mecha class; it includes both Brain Powerds and Grand Chers. Plural 'Antibodies'.
entries.notes: Every source agrees. The existing research notes already use 'Antibody'.

entries.role: The large rainbow disc plates that Orphan produces and that spawn Antibodies. Plural 'B-Plates'.
entries.notes: mmecha writes 'B-Plates'. No canonical wiki page exists.

entries.role: Short name of Yuu Isami (伊佐未勇), the male lead; pilots Yuu Brain.
entries.personality: Brooding lone wolf who resents his scientist parents; comes to value life and fights to save his sister Quincy.
entries.notes: Matches the existing research entry 'Yuu Isami' / short 'Yuu' and the unit 'Yuu Brain'. Assumes the line refers to the Brain Powerd character, the only Yuu in ACE2's cast.

entries.series: Mobile Suit Gundam / Gundam 0083: Stardust Memory
entries.role: Earth Federation mirror-array superweapon that focuses sunlight. ACE2 Op 08 sub-mission 'Defending Solar System' (in 0083 it is the Solar System II).
entries.notes: Gundam Wiki page title. The Mk. II version is 'Solar System II' (ソーラ・システムII). Also called 'Solar Flare System' (old official site).

entries.role: Earth Federation Forces special task force of the UC 0090s (Amuro, Bright, Ra Cailum).
entries.notes: Page title on both the Gundam and SRW wikis. The existing gundam_uc.json already uses it.

entries.role: Real name of Gai Daigoji (ダイゴウジ・ガイ), the hot-blooded Aestivalis pilot.
entries.personality: Loud, hot-blooded Gekigangar otaku who insists 'Gai' is his soul's name and hates being called Yamada.
entries.notes: On the Nadesico wiki, 'Jiro Yamada' redirects to 'Gai Daigoji', and the page gives {{nihongo|Jiro Yamada|ヤマダ・ジロウ}}. Western order, matching 'Gai Daigoji' and 'Akito Tenkawa' in names.json. The SRW Wiki once writes 'Yamada Jiro' in Japanese order.

entries.ja: グラビティ・ブラスト
entries.role: The Nadesico's main gravity cannon (also used by Jovian ships and the X-Aestivalis).
entries.notes: The Nadesico wiki writes 'Gravity Blast Cannon' (infobox) or 'gravity blast cannon' (prose). The SRW Wiki writes 'gravity blast'. Use 'Gravity Blast' as the weapon name.

entries.ja: キング・オブ・ハート
entries.role: Shuffle Alliance title held by Domon Kasshu (formerly Master Asia).
entries.notes: Contested. The Gundam Wiki's Shuffle Alliance page writes {{nihongo|King of Heart|キング・オブ・ハート}}, which is literal to the katakana. The English dub and common usage say 'King of Hearts'. Kept 'King of Hearts' to match the existing gundam_wing_g.json Domon entry. Switch to 'King of Heart' project-wide if the wiki-title rule should win.

entries.role: Domon's older brother and a Neo Japan scientist; co-developer of the Ultimate Gundam, later the Devil Gundam's core unit.
entries.personality: Kind and gentle; loves his younger brother and taught him to have faith in others.
entries.notes: Gundam Wiki page title. Same surname spelling as 'Domon Kasshu' in names.json.

entries.role: Neo Japan scientist; father of Domon and Kyoji, co-creator of the Ultimate Gundam.
entries.notes: Gundam Wiki page title.

entries.ja: リリーナ・ドーリアン
entries.role: Female lead; heir of the Sanc Kingdom (real name Relena Peacecraft), Zechs's younger sister, and a pacifist leader.
entries.personality: Idealistic, determined pacifist; dignified and unafraid to confront soldiers.
entries.notes: Gundam Wiki page title. 'Relena Peacecraft' redirects to it; use that only for リリーナ・ピースクラフト.

entries.ja: プリベンター・ウインド
entries.role: Zechs Merquise's Preventer codename.
entries.notes: Listed as an alias in the Gundam Wiki's Milliardo Peacecraft infobox. Matches the existing 'Preventer' and the 'Preventer Fire' note for Noin.

entries.role: Kaine's mother, administrator of the colony Alucard; captured by Giganos and used as leverage against Kaine.
entries.notes: Wikipedia cast list. The episode title 'Totsunyû! Aoi Wakaba kyûshutsu' uses the same spelling. Surname matches 'Kaine Wakaba'.

entries.role: Eiji's father: a human astronaut, lost in deep space and found by the Grados, who opposes the invasion and programmed the Layzner's hidden AI Fouron.
entries.notes: He is from Layzner, not Dragonar. Wikipedia and the SRW Wiki both write 'Ken Asuka'.

entries.ja: ペンタゴナ・ワールド
entries.role: The five-planet Pentagona system where L-Gaim is set.
entries.notes: 'Pentagona World' is the official title of the first L-Gaim OVA (MAHQ). The SRW Wiki says 'the Pentagona System' in prose. names.json already has ペンタゴナ = 'Pentagona'.

entries.ja: アルバトロ・ナル・エイジ
entries.role: Protagonist Eiji Asuka's Grados name without the surname; half-Grados son of Ken Asuka who pilots the Layzner.
entries.notes: names.json has アルバトロ・ナル・エイジ・アスカ = 'Albatro Null Eiji Asuka' (Wikipedia nihongo). This is the same name without アスカ. The SRW Wiki writes 'Albatro Null'. Don't use 'Nal'.

entries.role: Supreme commander of the Zentradi main fleet.
entries.notes: Macross Wiki page title. The katakana here (ゴルグ) matches the title better than names.json's ゴル・ボドルザー, which is mapped to the same 'Golg Boddole Zer'. Don't use Robotech's 'Dolza'.

entries.role: The beauty contest Lynn Minmay wins (SDF Macross ep. 9).
entries.notes: Macross Wiki page titles ('Miss Macross' is the episode, 'Miss Macross Contest' the event).

entries.ja: ガーディアン・システム
entries.role: System on the Ark-series units (Gun Ark, Buster Ark) that calls strikes from the Guardian military satellites.
entries.notes: This is ACE2-original, not Dragonar. It matches the existing macross_ace_original.json note (ガーディアンシステム = 'Guardian System') and names.json ガーディアン = 'Guardian'.

entries.role: Drake Luft's knight commander and Show Zama's former superior and rival; later fights masked as the Black Knight (黒騎士).
entries.personality: Proud and capable commander respected by his men; grows obsessed with defeating Show after repeated humiliation.
entries.notes: The SRW Wiki character list bolds 'Burn Bunnings'. Wikipedia writes 'Burne Bannings' and MAHQ 'Bern'. There is no page title. This follows the variants already noted in dunbine_rean_brain.json, where the Black Knight entry warns that his identity is a spoiler.

entries.ja: トランス・フォーメーション
entries.role: The SDF-1 Macross's transformation from cruiser mode to its humanoid attack mode; also the title of SDF Macross episode 5.
entries.notes: The Macross Wiki page 'Transformation' is episode 5, written トランス•フォーメーション with the same mid-dot split. Translate as 'Transformation'; use 'Trans-Formation' only if the game is clearly stylizing it.
